sections.html:
Grand Island is the county seat of Hall County in central Nebraska, a few miles north of the Platte River at about 1,870 feet in elevation. It was the fourth-largest city in the state at the 2020 census. Interstate 80 runs about 4 miles south of the city, U.S. 30 runs east and west through the center, and U.S. 281 is the main north-south route on the west edge. Central Nebraska Regional Airport is in town.

Grand Island has no fixed-route public transit. The local system is entirely demand-responsive, with rides booked 24 hours ahead, so daily life here runs on cars. When you describe your house to a buyer, mention garage space, driveway width and the distance to Highway 281 or I-80.

Grand Island averages about 26.6 inches of precipitation and 27.7 inches of snow a year, and May is the wettest month at 4.70 inches. Records run from minus 34 degrees to 117 degrees. May and June bring the most rain, so look at grading near the foundation, sump pumps, window wells and crawl spaces before a buyer's inspector does.

Storm damage is part of local memory, going back to a set of tornadoes in 1980. If your house has had hail or wind repairs, keep the paperwork. A record of past repairs helps you answer disclosure questions honestly. More than 140 freight trains a day pass through, so a house near the tracks may draw questions from buyers.

sections.h2: Which school district covers Grand Island homes
sections.html:
All of the city is in Grand Island Public Schools, and Grand Island Senior High School is its comprehensive high school. Central Catholic High School and Heartland Lutheran High School are the private options.

One detail trips up some buyers. Northwest Public Schools has a facility, including Northwest High School, inside the city limits, but none of that district's taxing and attendance boundary covers any part of the city. Property near the edge of town can sit in a different district, so check the district on the county tax statement rather than relying on the street address.

sections.h2: Selling a house with code problems
sections.html:
Grand Island's code lets the Chief Building Official order an owner to make a dangerous building safe, and it requires written notice by first-class and certified mail to the owner of record. A separate Property Maintenance Code covers substandard conditions such as litter, weeds, debris and other hazards on the premises.

  • Building Services covers the city and a two-mile area around it, and enforces the 2021 International Residential Code with local amendments.
  • Inspections are scheduled at (308) 385-5325.
  • Rental owners must supply, install, maintain and test smoke detectors.

If you hold a house with open code issues, ask the city what is outstanding before you set a price. A cash buyer will account for the work, while a financed buyer's lender may not accept the house until it is fixed. You can sell with open issues, but the city can still send notice to the owner of record, so tell the buyer in writing.

Hall County has fewer than 100,000 people, so it uses the standard schedule: taxes are due December 31, the first half is delinquent May 1 and the second half September 1.

DateWhat happens
January 1Real property is assessed
June 1The assessor mails notices of valuation changes
June 30Deadline for a protest and for a homestead exemption application
October 15Levy date
December 31Taxes are due
May 1 and September 1First and second halves become delinquent

The Hall County Treasurer, in Suite 2 of the same building as the Register of Deeds, also publishes a delinquent tax list each year. Check it for your parcel before you list.

sections.h2: Deeds and the Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Hall County records deeds through the Register of Deeds, at 200 South Sycamore Street, Suite 6, where the County Assessor is the contact. Every deed that is recorded must come with the Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521. The county's GIS viewer shows ownership and sale history for each parcel, which helps you check your own record before a buyer does.

The state documentary stamp tax on the seller is $3.32 per $1,000 for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026.

sections.h2: What the seller disclosure must cover
sections.html:
Nebraska Revised Statute 76-2,120 requires the statement to describe the condition of appliances that stay with the house, the electrical, heating, cooling, water and sewer systems, hazardous conditions, title matters such as easements and encroachments, utility connections, and compliance with carbon monoxide alarm rules. Any private transfer fee obligation must also be disclosed.

You may mark an item unknown if you truly do not know, and the statute protects a seller from liability for errors outside personal knowledge. It does not allow hiding something you know about. If a buyer does not receive the statement, they can recover damages, costs and attorney's fees.

Ask the Treasurer for the balance on the parcel, then give the number to the title company so it is paid from your proceeds. A delinquent half does not stop a sale, but it needs to be on the payoff list before the closing date is set.

faqs.q: When are Hall County property taxes due and delinquent?
faqs.a: Taxes are due December 31. For a county under 100,000 people, the first half is delinquent on May 1 and the second half on September 1.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Hall County valuation?
faqs.a: June 30 is the deadline for an individual real property protest, and the assessor sends valuation change notices by June 1.

faqs.q: Is Grand Island's whole city in one school district?
faqs.a: Yes. The city lies within Grand Island Public Schools, although a Northwest Public Schools facility sits inside the city limits without the district's taxing boundary covering any of it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Grand Island house that has code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners can sell with open issues, but the city can still send a written notice to the owner of record, so find out what is outstanding and tell the buyer in writing.

faqs.q: Who pays the Nebraska deed tax when a house is sold in Grand Island?
faqs.a: The grantor, meaning the seller. For deeds recorded from July 18, 2026, the rate is $3.32 per $1,000 of value, collected by the Hall County Register of Deeds.
